The plaintiff has been able to establish on record that the defendant has been running a canteen by the name of "Bhootpurv Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen".
The name of the canteen of the defendant on the face of it appears to be deceptively similar to that of the registered mark of the plaintiffs.
It is again a matter of record that the consumers of both plaintiffs and defendant are same set of persons.

I find substance in the submission of learned counsel for the plaintiffs that from the standpoint of an average purchaser with imperfect recollection, the overall similarity in sound and structure of trade name of defendant is likely to cause confusion or deception and mere etymological or lexical differences are considered immaterial.

In case reported as, "(1972) 1 SCC 618", titled as, "Parle Products (P)
Limited V/s J.P & Co., Mysore", the Hon'ble Supreme Court has been pleased to lay down the test for deceptive similarity in trademark infringement.

entities.text:
Parle Products (P)
Limited V/s J.P & Co., Mysore
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The dispute concerned the plaintiff's registered trademark and distinctive packaging for "Glucose Biscuits" and the defendant's use of similar packaging and get-up for their biscuits marketed under the name "Glucobiscuit".

The Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that the two marks, taken with their overall packaging and presentation, were deceptively similar - particularly given the class of consumers targeted, namely children and the general public, who are not expected to conduct a detailed comparison.
It was held that an average consumer, possessing imperfect recollection, could easily be misled due to the visual, phonetic, and structural similarities in the competing products.

Accordingly, the Hon'ble Supreme Court ruled in favour of the plaintiff and restrained the CS (Comm) No.184/2023: Ardh Sainik Canteen & Anr. V/s Bhhotpurv Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen/ Ex.Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen: DOD: 28.10.2025 defendant from continuing use of the impugned mark.

"9. It is therefore clear that in order to come to the conclusion whether one mark is deceptively similar to another, the broad and essential features of the two are to be considered.
They should not be placed side by side to find out if there are any differences in the design and if so, whether they are of such character as to prevent one design from being mistaken for the other.
It would be enough if the impugned mark bears such an overall similarity to the registered mark as would be likely to mislead a person usually dealing with one to accept the other if offered to him.

In this case we find that the packets are practically of the same size, the color scheme of the Ardh Sainik Canteen vs Bhhotpurv Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen on 28 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7367288/

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is clear that plaintiff No.1 is an unnecessary party, however, Mark B read with Ex.PW1/1 clearly establishes on record that plaintiff No.2 is the proprietor of mark "Ardh Sainik Canteen" having trademark .
The plaintiff has been able to establish on record that the defendant has been running a canteen by the name of "Bhootpurv Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen".
The name of the canteen of the defendant on the face of it appears to be deceptively similar to that of the registered mark of the plaintiffs.
It is again a matter of record that the consumers of both plaintiffs and defendant are same set of persons.
I find substance in the submission of learned counsel for the plaintiffs that from the standpoint of an average purchaser with imperfect recollection, the overall similarity in sound and structure of trade name of defendant is likely to cause confusion or deception and mere etymological or lexical differences are considered immaterial.
Accordingly, the Hon'ble Supreme Court ruled in favour of the plaintiff and restrained the CS (Comm) No.184/2023: Ardh Sainik Canteen & Anr. V/s Bhhotpurv Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen/ Ex.Ardh Sainik Kalyan Canteen: DOD: 28.10.2025 defendant from continuing use of the impugned mark.
Therefore, the plaintiffs have been able to establish the infringement of their trademark by the defendant.
